# starter-cloudflare-saas

The Drydock golden starter: a small, opinionated Cloudflare SaaS that AI coding agents extend, and the fixture for Drydock's integration tests. Everything here runs locally and offline against Cloudflare's local simulators. **No Cloudflare account, token or login is needed or wanted.**

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers (module syntax), Wrangler 4.148.0, `nodejs_compat` |
| API | Hono, in `src/api/`, served under `/api/*` |
| Frontend | React Router 7 framework mode, SSR on the same Worker (`app/`) |
| Data | D1 (`DB`, SQL migrations in `migrations/`), KV (`KV`), R2 (`ATTACHMENTS`) |
| Tests | Vitest 4 + `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` (real workerd, real D1/KV/R2 simulators), Playwright 1.64 for e2e |
| Lint / types | Biome (lint), `tsc --noEmit`, `wrangler types` output committed |

## What is a stub

These exist so the product has the right shape. Replace them before shipping; do not build on their internals.

- **Auth** (`src/lib/auth.ts`, `src/api/auth.ts`, `/login`). `POST /api/auth/login` accepts **any email**. It works only when `ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=true` **and** `ENVIRONMENT` is not `production`; otherwise it returns 403. `ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN` is set only in `.dev.vars`, never in `wrangler.jsonc` (a test enforces that). The session cookie itself is real: an HMAC-SHA256 token signed with Web Crypto (`src/lib/session.ts`), stateless, 7-day expiry, no revocation.
- **Billing** (`src/api/billing.ts`). `POST /api/billing/checkout` returns a documented fake payload (`stub: true`, `provider: "stub"`, `checkoutUrl` on the unresolvable `.invalid` TLD) and an `X-Stub: billing` header. `GET /api/billing/status` always says `free`. No provider is connected.
- **Rate limit** (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`). A fixed-window counter in KV, applied to login. KV is eventually consistent and not atomic: it is a brake, not a security boundary.
- **Attachments** (`/api/items/:id/attachment`). One R2 object per item, 1 MiB, `text/plain`, PNG, JPEG or PDF only, always served with `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `nosniff`. There is no UI for it.

## Layout

```
workers/app.ts        Worker entry: /api/* -> Hono, everything else -> React Router
src/api/              Hono routes (app.ts wires them; index.ts is the API-only entry used by tests)
src/lib/              session, auth, items (D1), rate-limit; shared by API routes and page loaders
app/                  React Router routes (home = items, login, logout)
migrations/           D1 SQL migrations (0001_init.sql: users + items)
test/                 Vitest tests, run inside workerd
e2e/                  Playwright tests
scripts/              dev.mjs (ports), preview.mjs (D6 guard), previews-guard.mjs
worker-configuration.d.ts   generated by `wrangler types`; commit it
.drydock-fixtures/    intentionally broken patches for Drydock's integration tests (not applied)
```

## Commands

Each `task` target calls the npm script of the same name, so `npm run <name>` works wherever `task` is not installed.

| Task | npm script | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `task install` | `npm ci` | install exactly the locked versions (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`, see Notes) |
| `task build` | `npm run build` | production build into `build/` |
| `task test` | `npm test` | Vitest in workerd; also writes `test-results/vitest.json` |
| `task lint` | `npm run lint` | Biome; failures print as `::error file=...,line=...::message` |
| `task typecheck` | `npm run typecheck` | `react-router typegen`, `wrangler types --check`, `tsc --noEmit` (`file(line,col): error TSnnnn`) |
| `task types` | `npm run types` | regenerate `worker-configuration.d.ts` after changing `wrangler.jsonc` |
| `task migrate-local` | `npm run migrate:local` | apply D1 migrations to `.wrangler/state` |
| `task dev` | `npm run dev` | build if needed, migrate, then `wrangler dev` |
| `task e2e` | `npm run e2e` | Playwright; screenshots in `test-results/screenshots/` |
| `task preview` | `npm run preview` | `wrangler preview` only |

`build`, `test`, `lint` and `typecheck` exit 0 on success and non-zero on failure. Run `task check` for all four.

### Running several worktrees at once

`wrangler dev` state lives in `.wrangler/state` inside each worktree, so databases are separate automatically (run `task migrate-local`, or just `task dev`, in a new worktree: it starts empty). Ports come from the environment:

```
PORT=8801 INSPECTOR_PORT=9301 task dev      # unset values pick free ports
PORT=8802 INSPECTOR_PORT=9302 task e2e      # e2e defaults to 8788 / 9230
```

`dev` prints `DRYDOCK_DEV_URL=http://localhost:<port>` for tooling to parse.

### First run

```
npm ci
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars   # optional: dev.mjs creates it if missing
task dev
```

### e2e browsers

`npx playwright install chromium` downloads from `cdn.playwright.dev`. Where that host is blocked, point Playwright at an installed Chromium: `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/path/to/chrome task e2e`.

## How agents should work here

1. Work in your own worktree; never edit `main` directly. Run `task check` before declaring anything done. A claim of completion is not evidence; the checks are.
2. Change behaviour test-first where you can. API behaviour belongs in `test/*.test.ts` (use `login()` and `api()` from `test/helpers.ts`); user flows belong in `e2e/`.
3. Schema changes are **new** migration files (`migrations/0002_*.sql`). Never edit an applied migration. Add a test, then `task migrate-local`.
4. After editing `wrangler.jsonc`, run `task types` and commit `worker-configuration.d.ts`; `task typecheck` fails when it is stale.
5. Keep every D1 query scoped by `user_id` and parameterised (`.bind(...)`). Treat request bodies, uploaded files and cookies as untrusted.
6. Do not add production secrets, tokens or real resource ids anywhere. Local secrets go in `.dev.vars` (gitignored).
7. Do not create `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `GEMINI.md` here: Drydock generates and owns them.

## D6: preview and production separation

Cloudflare is an agent-side template in Drydock (decision D6), not Drydock's own infrastructure. Rules for any project built from this starter:

- **Agents never run `wrangler deploy`** (or `versions deploy`, `rollback`, `delete`, or any production-affecting command). The agent-process allowlist should permit only `wrangler dev`, `wrangler types`, `wrangler d1 ... --local` and `wrangler preview` (plus `wrangler versions upload` where previews are unavailable). No production token may exist in an agent process.
- The only deployment-shaped command is `task preview` (`scripts/preview.mjs`). It first checks that the `previews` block of `wrangler.jsonc` shares no D1 database, KV namespace or R2 bucket with production and rebinds all of them, then runs exactly `wrangler preview` with a fixed option allowlist.
- The top-level bindings in `wrangler.jsonc` are production; the `previews` block binds **separate** resources under the same binding names. Never copy a production id into `previews`. Previews do not isolate services, routes, cron triggers, Workflows or queue consumers: do not add those without giving previews their own copy.
- Cloudflare API tokens cannot tell "upload a preview" from "go live" (both need Workers Scripts Write), so the real boundary is an account boundary (a separate Cloudflare account, or none, for previews) plus the command allowlist, not a token scope. CI uses `CF_PREVIEW_API_TOKEN` (and `CF_PREVIEW_ACCOUNT_ID`) from that account; the preview job is skipped when the secret is absent.
- `wrangler versions upload` Version URLs reuse the **production** bindings. `npm run preview -- --versions` therefore refuses to run unless `ALLOW_VERSIONS_UPLOAD=1`. Prefer `wrangler preview`.
- Preview URLs are public by default, and dev login is off there (`ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN` is `"false"` in `wrangler.jsonc`), so a preview cannot be signed into until real auth exists.
- The ids in `wrangler.jsonc` are placeholders (`REPLACE_WITH_...`). Local development and tests never read them.

## Notes

- `.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps=true`: npm 10's resolver crashes on Vitest's optional peers with this tree. All dependency versions are pinned exactly in `package.json`.
- `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` is deprecated in favour of `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin`, which this starter uses (same API, and it shares the Wrangler 4.148.0 install).
- `wrangler dev` logs a harmless "Unable to fetch the `Request.cf` object" warning when offline.
- `.drydock-fixtures/*.patch` are unified diffs for Drydock's integration tests (`break-test.patch` fails one API test, `break-types.patch` introduces a type error). Apply with `patch -p1 < .drydock-fixtures/<name>.patch` from the project root. They are never applied to this tree.
